topic: Advanced Python Architecture with Type Hints, Dataclasses, and Pydantic
learningObjectives: Apply type hints to make Python code clearer and safer.
Use dataclasses to model structured application data.
Create validated data models with Pydantic.

activities.title: Type Hint Anatomy
activities.instruction: Click each annotated part of the function to understand its meaning.

content.concept: Type hints describe expected parameter and return types. Python does not generally enforce these annotations at runtime by itself, but tools such as type checkers can use them to detect problems.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

items: def calculate_total(price: float, quantity: int) -> float:
descriptions: Defines a function with annotated parameters and an annotated return type.
Indicates that price is expected to be a floating-point value.
Indicates that quantity is expected to be an integer.
Indicates that the function is expected to return a floating-point value.

activities.instruction: Choose the validation rule that best fits the field.

content.concept: Pydantic models define fields and constraints for external data and can validate and parse incoming values according to the model definition.

activities.title: Data Modeling Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the approach that best fits the requirement.

content.concept: Type hints improve code clarity and tooling, dataclasses are convenient for structured Python objects, and Pydantic models are especially useful when validating or parsing external data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Use type hints when documenting expected types in application code
Use a dataclass for a simple internal data container
Use a Pydantic model for validating API request data
Use an untyped dictionary for every external request
config.answer: Use a Pydantic model for validating API request data
